description: Sound it out on ταῦτα for a reader whose English accent is British (the request says so, and its guide keys the o to the British word): the explanation still describes αυ by the app's respelling, TAF-ta, never as aw, and any English example is a British one.

request.greek: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν πρὸς ταῦτα Εἰ ὁ θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τίς καθ' ἡμῶν
request.english: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
request.question: The word ταῦτα (lemma οὗτος; demonstrative pronoun, accusative plural neuter) in Romans 8:31. Help me pronounce this word: its syllables and how each sounds.
request.pronunciation_guide: Modern Greek, as Greek is spoken in Greece today: never by English spelling habit and never by the Erasmian (school) pronunciation. The app respells a word in syllables, the stressed one in capitals: ταῦτα is TAF-ta, Πάντοτε is PAN-do-te, χαίρετε is HYE-re-te. The vowels, each with a word of the reader's English that has it: a as in father; e as in pet; ee as in see; o as in lot; oo as in food. αυ and ευ are af and ef before θ κ ξ π σ τ φ χ ψ, and av and ev before a voiced consonant or a vowel (never "aw", never "ow"); ηυ is eef or eev the same way. αι is e; ει, οι, υι, η, ι and υ are ee; ου is oo; ω and ο are o. β is v; δ is dh, the th of “this”; γ is gh (or y before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι); θ is th as in thin; φ is f; ρ is r, lightly rolled; χ is kh as in loch, the Scottish ch, before α, ο, ω, ου or a consonant, and the softer hy before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι. μπ, ντ and γκ are b, d and g at the start of a word and mb, nd and ng inside it; γγ is ng; γχ is ng plus kh (or hy before ε, ι, η, υ, αι, ει or οι); γξ is nks. σ is z before β γ δ ζ λ μ ν ρ. A doubled consonant is said once. Both breathings are silent, and the iota under a letter is not said.
